author: cskiraly
content:
I was running discv5 only kurtosis tests in preparation for turning off discv4 support. Here are the results and some observations: 
```
| Client | joins discv5 mesh | supports discv5 only | discv5-only flag | discv5 from enode | discv5 from ENR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| geth | ✅ 5 | ✅ | `--discovery.v4=false` | ✅ | ✅ |
| nethermind | ✅ 5 | ✅ | `--Discovery.DiscoveryVersion V5` | ✅ | ✅ |
| ethrex | ✅ 5 | ✅ | `--p2p.discv4=false` | ✅ | ✅ |
| erigon | ✅ 5 | ✅ | `--discovery.v4=false` | ❌ | ✅ |
| besu | ✅ 5 | ❌ | `--Xv5-discovery-enabled=true` (adds v5, keeps v4) | ❌ (enode→discv4) | ✅ |
| nimbus-eth1 | ✅ 5 | ❌ | `--discv5=true` (all-or-nothing) | ❌ (enode→discv4) | ✅ |
| reth | ❌ | ✅ flag, unusable | `--disable-discv4-discovery` | ❌ | ❌ |
```

- by default kurtosis is serving EL bootnodes as "enode", not as "ENR".  Only **geth/nethermind/ethrex** actually bootstrap discv5 from a bare **enode**; erigon, besu, nimbus and reth need an **ENR** for discv5. I had to patch to serve ENRs.
- I had to play around with the bootnode in kurtosis to make this work. Now there are 3 options (still in PRs):
   - use bootnodoor (open PR to support erigon)
   - use an EL client as bootnode (geth by default (in a PR)
   - use the geth devp2p tool as a bootnode (in a PR)

After these workarounds 3 issues remain:
- <@&836981603216654336> and <@&595681804422479873> has no option to turn off discv4 support. Please add it (I think there is already a merged PR for besu, maybe just not on the branch I've used).
- <@&1070471163219824730> fails to connect, please check and correct

author: deme1744
content:
Regarding the discv5 from enode. I would **really** prefer not to have to add that. I consider enode equally obsolete as discv4. And I've always considered discv5 from enode a hack. It defeats the purpose of ENRs.
Kurtosis should support ENRs and it should be the default. In fact, ENR to enode makes way more sense for keeping some backwards compatibility.
